correctness.rationale: Uniform large negative shocks force entry below -L from all states; positive noise tail failures along the quadratic descent threshold have total probability <=64v/(15r^2 L^4) <=1/2. Uniform conditional escape probability is upgraded to one by martingale convergence. Stationarity contradicts almost sure divergence. The bounded comparator has an explicit invariant interval and a W1 contraction, hence a unique stationary law there. Exact rational example and quartic signs independently checked by bundled code.

originality.rationale: The Gaussian unbounded-noise logistic escape and bounded-noise positive attractors are known from Bassols-Cornudella--Lamb (2023) and earlier bounded-noise literature, so neither is claimed alone. The motivating Yang--Han model addresses only a formal Gaussian moment-closure equilibrium. The new claim is the universally quantified, finite-second-moment, one-sided unbounded-negative-tail theorem for all r>0 and the exact same-variance non-Gaussian contrasting stationary/escaping processes. value.rationale: The primary applied question is whether mean-zero fluctuations with the same finite variance yield an actual positive stationary population. The theorem gives a full distribution-class obstruction, an explicit positive invariant-regime counterpoint at the same variance, and an exact two-root formal-closure instance where moment methods cannot identify the stationary regime. This distinguishes genuinely asymptotic population persistence from metastable finite-window simulations without changing the source closure equations. The all-r/all-law mechanism and matching non-Gaussian example are substantive, not merely a negative-boundary domain check.
